record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: compact CDH spaces of weight c
record.original_question: Does ZFC prove the existence of a compact countable dense homogeneous space of weight equal to the continuum c?

evidence.quote: Problem 30 (Hernández–Hrušák–van Mill [43]). Is there (in ZFC) a compact CDH space of weight c?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if $X$ is separable and for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. The weight of a topological space $X$, denoted $w(X)$, is the smallest cardinality of a base for the topology of $X$. Let $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the cardinality of the continuum.

Question: Does ZFC prove the existence of a compact Hausdorff countable dense homogeneous space $X$ with $w(X) = \mathfrak{c}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is attributed to Hernández-Hrušák-van Mill and is listed as an open problem in surveys on countable dense homogeneity. While related work has established (in ZFC) the existence of compact non-metrizable CDH spaces, the specific question of producing a compact CDH space of weight exactly $\mathfrak{c}$ in ZFC appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and lambda-sets
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses compact CDH spaces; raises question on existence of compact CDH space of weight c in ZFC.
status_evidence.claim: The question on existence in ZFC of a compact CDH space of weight c is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on CDH that still references open problems concerning compact CDH spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to treat the compact CDH weight-c question as unresolved.
